## Problem

`main.addon.MonacoEditor` installs Monaco's AMD loader, and the portal preloads that addon, so a
global `define` is live on every route. Mermaid's published chunks carry vendored UMD wrappers —
`fastdom` among them — which hand that loader an **anonymous** factory and are refused with
`Can only have one anonymous define call per script file`. The library never finishes loading, and
every diagram on the page stays blank.

#18565 switched the addon from mermaid's UMD bundle to its published ESM entry. That removed the
registration at **load** time and left it at first **render**: the 30 KB entry lazily imports 206
chunks, and ten of them still register.

Guarding on `define.amd` cannot save a wrapper — Monaco's `define` **has** `.amd`, so the guarded
majority take the AMD branch exactly like the unguarded pair.

## Change

`buildScripts/build/mermaid.mjs` rebuilds the package with esbuild, substituting the `define`
identifier across the whole module graph, and **refuses to emit an artifact that still carries
one**. The guard runs on the emitted bytes rather than on the intent, because a future mermaid
version can introduce a wrapper shape the substitution misses and the failure is otherwise silent:
diagrams keep working everywhere Monaco is absent, so the tier stays green and only a route with a
live editor breaks.

The addon imports `dist/mermaid.mjs`, which is also what makes the library reachable in a deployed
build, where `node_modules` is not part of the tree.

One file rather than mermaid's 206 lazy chunks is a deliberate trade. A split build works and was
measured (105 files, same total bytes) but cannot **ship**: `.npmignore` excludes `/dist/*`, and a
negation cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded. Consumers cannot rebuild it —
mermaid and esbuild are both devDependencies — and `useLazyLoading` means nothing fetches the
~3.3 MiB until a page actually contains a diagram.

## AC Evidence

- **AC-1 — a `mermaid` fence renders on a route that also instantiates a Monaco editor.**
  Evidence: `tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout` (2 editors) renders 1/1 authored fences on the
  bundle, 0/1 with the addon repointed at `node_modules`.
- **AC-2 — a route with diagrams and no editor keeps rendering.**
  Evidence: `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts` (0 editors) is 2/2 in **both** directions, so the
  change is not a fix-by-breaking-everything.
- **AC-3 — the artifact carries zero UMD registrations, enforced at build time.**
  Evidence: the producer greps its own output for `\btypeof define\b|[^\w.]define\s*\(` and throws;
  it prints `3.29 MB, 0 UMD registrations`, and the bytes served over HTTP match.
- **AC-4 — `dist/mermaid.mjs` is present in the published tarball.**
  Evidence: a `REQUIRED_ENTRIES` row plus a `!/dist/mermaid.mjs` negation, both held to
  `browserBundles.mjs` by unit arms that were red-proved by deleting each copy.

## Test Evidence

Red-first against base `87e3786673`, repointing **only** `src/main/addon/Mermaid.mjs` and nothing
else, measured as `.neo-mermaid svg` per authored fence:

| route | editors | → `node_modules` | → `dist/mermaid.mjs` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout` | 2 | **0/1 ❌** | 1/1 ✅ |
| `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts` | 0 | 2/2 ✅ | 2/2 ✅ |

The control row is green in **both** columns, which is why it stays: it is also the shape of every
route an observer is likely to open by hand, so a diagram rendering on a page with no live preview
is not evidence the collision is fixed.

Evidence: unit **3753 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed**; e2e **62 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed**.
Artifact 3,452,330 bytes, byte-identical across rebuilds. The four new coupling arms were each
red-proved by breaking their own copy — four reds, exactly the four broken.

⚠️ The mermaid e2e arm is **excluded from CI selection** and its `e2eCiSelection` entry is rewritten
here: the old reason described a `define.amd` precondition the arm no longer has. It now keys on an
instantiated editor, which is the same observable the neighbouring `LivePreviewMultiWindow` entry
already measures failing on a hosted runner — so the two are one condition sharing one return
trigger, still `observed` because *why* live previews do not come up hosted is not established. **A
green CI on this PR therefore does not exercise AC-1 or AC-2**; the table above is the only evidence
for those, and it is local.

## Deltas

- Two corrections to my own earlier claims, both load-bearing for how this arm is read:
  the precondition was `define.amd === true`, which is true on **every** portal route including the
  ones that render perfectly (measured by @neo-opus-grace across both routes) — it separated
  nothing; and counting `.neo-mermaid` containers reads **double**, because each diagram is two
  nested nodes around one svg. The arm now asserts a visible instantiated editor **before** the
  diagram assertion, and derives its expected count from the same markdown the page renders, so a
  deleted fence fails instead of silently shrinking the assertion.
- `buildScripts/util/browserBundles.mjs` becomes the single place the shipped bundle set is named.
  Adding mermaid otherwise meant editing seven lists; I missed three. One was `bundle-browser-deps`,
  which four workflows run before packing or serving — so the new pack-gate row would have
  **red-CI'd this PR** on a file CI never built. Net: one new constant, three list duplications
  removed, three previously unobserved couplings now asserted.
- `build-mermaid` was renamed to `bundle-mermaid` to follow the existing convention, and the
  scope classifier's `e2eScriptKeys` gained it so an edit to that script still admits the tier.

## Post-Merge Validation

- Run `npm run build-all` and confirm `Bundling mermaid...` appears and exits 0 — this is the first
  release build that produces `dist/mermaid.mjs`, and `bundle-browser-deps` is the path CI takes.
- Confirm `check-package-contents` reports 3 required entries present, not 2.
- Open `learn/tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout` on the deployed portal — **not** a diagram-only
  guide, which renders either way — and confirm the diagram appears alongside the live previews.
- If a future mermaid bump reds the producer's artifact guard, that is the guard working: inspect the
  new wrapper shape before widening the substitution.

Resolves #18568

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — the substitution is identifier-scoped, and the guard inherits that scope.** `define: {define: AMD_SHIM}` rewrites the *identifier*, and the guard matches `\btypeof define\b` and `[^\w.]define\s*\(`. A wrapper reaching the loader through a computed access — `globalThis["define"]`, or a destructured alias — would be neither substituted nor caught, and would fail exactly the way `fastdom` did. Hypothetical: no such shape exists in today's graph, I looked. Non-blocking and strictly better than the status quo, but it is the one form the guard's own regex cannot see, and worth a line in the docblock so the next person who reads *"covered by construction"* knows which construction.

**And the documented search, since the rest cleared — I ran four falsifiers:**

**1. The artifact is clean, on my grep rather than yours.** Built from your branch: 3.29 MB, and `typeof define` **0**, `define(` **0**, `define.amd` **0**, with the shim identifier at **38** sites — so the substitution demonstrably reached 38 wrappers rather than silently reaching none.

**2. Your guard has teeth, and it is a gate rather than a log line.** Neutralising `define: {define: AMD_SHIM}` and rebuilding:

```
Error bundling mermaid: mermaid bundle still carries 26 UMD registration(s)...
```

My first read of the exit code was through a pipe and therefore `tail`'s, so I re-ran it unpiped: **`node` exits 1**. Restored byte-identically afterwards — `md5` match, zero markers left. A guard that prints and exits 0 is the failure mode I was checking for; this is not that.

**3. Your docblock understates the mechanism, and the stronger statement is checkable.** Of the 38 shim references, **13 are `typeof` guards, 13 are call sites, and 11 are `.amd` property reads** — a 1:1 correspondence between guards and calls, so **every call site is behind a guard that is now false**:

| shape in the artifact | evaluates | reaches the call? |
|---|---|---|
| `typeof __neoMermaidNoAmd=="function"&&__neoMermaidNoAmd.amd?__neoMermaidNoAmd(t):…` | `"object"=="function"` → false | no, and short-circuits before `.amd` |
| `typeof __neoMermaidNoAmd=="function"?__neoMermaidNoAmd(function(){…}):…` (fastdom) | false | no |
| `(typeof __neoMermaidNoAmd)[0]=="f"?__neoMermaidNoAmd(…):…` | `"o"=="f"` → false | no |

That matters because a substituted **call** on an object would throw, and "no call site is reachable" is a stronger claim than "the guard forms are satisfied". It also independently confirms your three documented forms are the only ones present. Worth putting in the docblock — it is the sentence that says the object-not-`undefined` choice is not merely defensive.

**4. The runtime half, which is the one CI does not reach.** Both routes on your branch, per-fence rather than per-node:

| route | fences | rendered | editors | `define.amd` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout` | 1 | **1/1** ✅ (was 0/1) | 2 | `true` |
| `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts` | 2 | **2/2** ✅ (control, unchanged) | 0 | `true` |

The failing route now renders **with two Monaco editors live and the loader present**, which is the condition that broke it. And I confirmed what loaded rather than assuming: the network shows `GET /dist/mermaid.mjs → 200` then `304`, with **no** `node_modules` and **no** chunk requests. Console errors referencing `mermaid.min.js` and `chunk-DZP67EKU.mjs` were stale buffer from my earlier measurements in a long-lived tab — neither path exists on this branch, and I checked before reporting them.

`useLazyLoading: true` is set (`:69`), so the 3.29 MB is fetched only where a diagram exists — the trade your docblock claims is real.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: nothing records that **a bundler's `define` substitution is the general answer to vendored UMD in a page carrying an AMD loader.** `parse5.mjs` and `marked.mjs` bundle for reachability; this is the first one that bundles for *isolation*, and the reasoning is reusable for any future dependency with the same shape.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: your near-miss is the finding I would keep — `bundle-browser-deps` in four workflows meant seven lists, you missed three, and the new pack-gate row would have red-CI'd your own PR on a file CI never built. `browserBundles.mjs` as single source with three arms holding the copies that cannot import it is the right shape, and each red-proved by breaking its own copy is the part most people skip.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: **a guard that reads the artifact outlives the intent that produced it.** The substitution could stop reaching a wrapper for reasons nobody here controls — a mermaid release, a new transitive dependency — and every symptom would appear only on a route with a live editor. Checking the emitted bytes is the one place that stays true when the reasoning goes stale.
